title: The ASPLOS 2025 / EuroSys 2025 Contest on Intra-Operator Parallelism for Distributed Deep Learning
problem: Selecting the optimal intra-operator parallelism strategy (how to partition and distribute each operation in a neural network across multiple accelerators) is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem that significantly impacts distributed training and inference performance.
motivation: As models grow larger and clusters more heterogeneous, automatic parallelism strategy search becomes critical to unlocking maximum hardware utilization; no single prior method dominates across diverse architectures.
method: The organizers created a benchmark suite—a set of test problems using real neural network operations—and asked participants to develop algorithms that decide how to split each operation across multiple accelerators (specialized computers for AI) to minimize total execution time. Over several months, competitors submitted their solutions and were evaluated on this benchmark. The paper then examined the problem structure, how the benchmark was designed, the key challenges participants faced (like the combinatorial explosion of possible ways to split operations), and how well different solutions performed.
key_novelty: A structured community competition and benchmark suite that revealed how far current techniques are from solving the problem of splitting neural network operations optimally across multiple accelerators.
contributions: A formal problem formulation for intra-operator parallelism strategy selection in distributed deep learning.
A new benchmark suite covering diverse neural network operator types and cluster configurations.
A retrospective analysis of competition submissions revealing the current state-of-the-art and open challenges.
Identification of key algorithmic opportunities for improving model partitioning in heterogeneous clusters.

metrics.other: benchmark quality of partitioning algorithm submissions

baselines: prior model partitioning algorithms (unnamed in abstract)
limitations: Not a system paper; does not provide a single novel system contribution or quantitative performance result.
primary_theme: Community contest and benchmark for intra-operator parallelism strategy search
